scope.current_boundary: Define power as work done or energy transferred per unit time, relate power to work and time via P = W/t = Delta E/t, understand the watt and its SI base units, and analyze power on graphs and through efficiency. Do not pre-teach the derivation and application of P = Fv, which is reserved for lesson 9702_t05_cm01_l04.

immediate_previous.boundary: Efficiency as ratio of useful energy output to total energy input.
can_assume: concept of work done W = Fs
efficiency as useful energy output / total energy input

immediate_next.boundary: Problem solving with power, derivation and application of P = Fv, vehicles moving at constant speed against resistance.
must_not_preteach: derivation of P = Fv from W = Fs and v = s/t
applications of P = Fv to cars, trains, and aircraft at constant speed
cubic drag power law P proportional to v^3

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Informed the core distinction that power is fundamentally work done divided by time taken, linking force times displacement per unit time.
question_parts_inspected.assessed_demand: Select the correct conceptual derivation linking power, work done, force, and velocity.
question_parts_inspected.reasoning_or_distractor: Option A is correct: power = work / time = (force * displacement) / time. Distractors invert multiplication by time or confuse distance and displacement.

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Informed the requirement to emphasize time conversion into seconds and proper treatment of power output over power input.
question_parts_inspected.assessed_demand: Calculate the ratio of power output to power input given fuel consumption in litres per hour and energy density in MJ per litre.
question_parts_inspected.reasoning_or_distractor: Distractors omit conversion of hours to seconds (3600) or misplace metric prefixes (mega- and kilo-).
